title: Step-language characterization
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S$ be a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$, and $sp(\lvert x\rvert)\le S$. If $C$ is a reachable configuration on input $x$, then, for every natural number $c'$, the encoding of $x$, the code of $C$ at space bound $S$, the number $c'$, and $S$ belongs to the step language of $N$ if and only if there is a choice bit $b\in\{0,1\}$ such that $c'$ is the code at space bound $S$ of the configuration obtained by taking choice $b$ from $C$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ uses at most $sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$
